jove-epoxidation.says: concerted syn addition: a cis alkene gives a cis epoxide and a trans alkene a trans epoxide

ucla-pcc.cite: UCLA Illustrated Glossary of Organic Chemistry: PCC

corrections.note: Regiochemistry counted an unlisted coproduct (methanol from DIBAL reduction) as a stray 'major'. Now only products the case lists (major, minor, forbidden) can make a verdict wrong.
Expected product changed from benzoic acid to the benzoate anion (the sourced product is sodium benzoate).
The registry-claim pattern included the word 'oxygen' and matched unrelated oxidation rules; narrowed to Wacker/PdCl.
Expected ester stereochemistry was written as retention; corrected to inversion, (R).
For stereo-specified unsupported cases only new tetrahedral centres ('@') count; a retained alkene geometry ('/') no longer counts as stereochemistry being specified.
Allow-list extended with benzylic-allylic-alcohol-oxidation after review.

Run 3 onward: an unsupported case whose reference structure also arises from an unrelated rule (Fischer for the Mitsunobu ester, mCPBA epoxidation for the Sharpless epoxide) is 'other-rule-match', not 'supported-correct', because no rule claims the reagent system; stereo-labelled expectations are scored for such matches too.
